description:
We researched colibri (JustVugg/colibri) — a pure-C MoE inference engine with an OpenAI-compatible API that runs models without a GPU.

We created `scripts/run_colibri.sh`, a bash wrapper around colibri's `coli` launcher, designed for headless servers with `install/start/serve/stop/status/logs/chat/doctor/update/unit` actions.

The script is pre-flight safe: it checks RAM, disk space and compiler availability before downloading, with sensible server defaults (`0.0.0.0:8000`, `~/colibri`, `~/colibri-models`).

It starts with the smallest models that fit entirely in RAM: `qwen36-35b` (23 GB, default), `qwen3-coder-30b` (19 GB) and `olmoe` (14 GB), instead of the 180–430 GB disk-streaming ones.

Next step is to run `chmod +x scripts/run_colibri.sh`, then `install`, `start`, and optionally generate a systemd unit for production.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ==============================================================================
#  run_colibri.sh — run colibri (https://github.com/JustVugg/colibri) on a server
# ==============================================================================
#  colibri runs large Mixture-of-Experts models on ordinary hardware: the dense
#  part of the model stays in RAM, the routed experts stream from disk. It is
#  pure C, needs no GPU and exposes an OpenAI-/Anthropic-compatible HTTP API.
#
#  This script is a thin wrapper around colibri's own launcher (`coli`):
#  it clones the repo, installs a SMALL model first, and runs the server.
#
#  QUICK START (small models)
#      chmod +x scripts/run_colibri.sh
#      scripts/run_colibri.sh install     # clone + build engine + download model
#      scripts/run_colibri.sh start       # background server on 0.0.0.0:8000
#      scripts/run_colibri.sh status      # is it up? which URLs?
#
#  SMALL MODELS (whole model fits in RAM, no disk streaming)
#      qwen36-35b       Qwen3.6-35B-A3B    23 GB   10/20 GB RAM   chat + thinking + tools  (default)
#      qwen3-coder-30b  Qwen3-Coder-30B    19 GB    8/18 GB RAM   code + tool calls, no thinking
#      olmoe            OLMoE-7B           14 GB    8 GB RAM      smallest; needs a GGUF->int8
#                                                                conversion (manual, see docs)
#  Bigger models are only a `--model` away: `scripts/run_colibri.sh list --all`
#  (they stream experts from the SSD, so a fast NVMe is what makes them usable).
#
#  ACTIONS
#      install       clone/pull colibri, check the machine, build engine, download model
#      start         start the server in the background (uses the saved config)
#      serve         run the server in the FOREGROUND (for systemd / docker / tmux)
#      stop          stop the background server
#      restart       stop + start
#      status        what is installed, is the server up, which URLs
#      logs          last lines of the server log (and of the install log)
#      chat          interactive terminal chat with the installed model
#      doctor        read-only health check (model files, compiler, permissions)
#      plan          where the model will live: RAM / VRAM / disk
#      list          every model of the catalog against this machine
#      update        git pull + rebuild + restart
#      reconfigure   choose another model / another backend
#      unit          print a ready-to-use systemd unit for `serve`
#      help          this text
#
#  ENVIRONMENT (all optional, sensible server defaults)
#      COLIBRI_HOME          checkout folder            (default: ~/colibri)
#      COLIBRI_MODELS_DIR    where models are stored    (default: ~/colibri-models)
#      COLIBRI_MODEL         catalog id to install      (default: qwen36-35b)
#      COLIBRI_HOST          bind address               (default: 0.0.0.0)
#      COLIBRI_PORT          port                       (default: 8000)
#      COLIBRI_BACKEND       auto|cpu|vulkan|cuda       (default: auto)
#      COLIBRI_API_KEY       bearer token the API requires (default: empty = no auth)
#      COLIBRI_ALLOWED_HOSTS extra Host headers accepted (comma separated)
#      COLIBRI_CORS_ORIGINS  allowed CORS origins       (comma separated)
#      COLIBRI_KV_SLOTS      conversations served at once (default: 1)
#      COLIBRI_MODEL_DIR     use an already downloaded model instead of detecting it
#      COLIBRI_FORCE=1       skip the RAM / disk pre-flight checks
#
#  Real examples:
#      COLIBRI_MODEL=qwen3-coder-30b scripts/run_colibri.sh install
#      COLIBRI_API_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 24) scripts/run_colibri.sh start
#      scripts/run_colibri.sh chat --topp 0.85        # extra args go to `coli chat`
#
#  Colibri docs: https://github.com/JustVugg/colibri
# ==============================================================================

set -Eeuo pipefail

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ configuration
COLIBRI_REPO="${COLIBRI_REPO:-https://github.com/JustVugg/colibri.git}"
COLIBRI_HOME="${COLIBRI_HOME:-${HOME}/colibri}"
COLIBRI_MODELS_DIR="${COLIBRI_MODELS_DIR:-${HOME}/colibri-models}"
COLIBRI_MODEL="${COLIBRI_MODEL:-qwen36-35b}"
COLIBRI_HOST="${COLIBRI_HOST:-0.0.0.0}"
COLIBRI_PORT="${COLIBRI_PORT:-8000}"
COLIBRI_BACKEND="${COLIBRI_BACKEND:-auto}"
COLIBRI_API_KEY="${COLIBRI_API_KEY:-}"
COLIBRI_KV_SLOTS="${COLIBRI_KV_SLOTS:-1}"
COLIBRI_ALLOWED_HOSTS="${COLIBRI_ALLOWED_HOSTS:-}"
COLIBRI_CORS_ORIGINS="${COLIBRI_CORS_ORIGINS:-}"
COLIBRI_MODEL_DIR="${COLIBRI_MODEL_DIR:-}"
COLIBRI_FORCE="${COLIBRI_FORCE:-0}"

# Where colibri's setup keeps its own run configuration, state and logs.
COLI_SETUP_HOME="${COLI_SETUP_HOME:-${XDG_DATA_HOME:-${HOME}/.local/share}/colibri}"

HB="colibri"
SCRIPT_NAME="$(basename "$0")"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers / output
if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
  C_RESET=$'\033[0m'; C_INFO=$'\033[0;36m'; C_OK=$'\033[0;32m'
  C_WARN=$'\033[0;33m'; C_ERR=$'\033[0;31m'; C_BOLD=$'\033[1m'
else
  C_RESET=""; C_INFO=""; C_OK=""; C_WARN=""; C_ERR=""; C_BOLD=""
fi

log()  { printf '%s[%s]%s %s\n' "$C_INFO" "$HB" "$C_RESET" "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '%s[%s]%s %s\n' "$C_OK"   "$HB" "$C_RESET" "$*"; }
warn() { printf '%s[%s]%s %s\n' "$C_WARN" "$HB" "$C_RESET" "$*" >&2; }
die()  { printf '%s[%s]%s %s\n' "$C_ERR"  "$HB" "$C_RESET" "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
step() { printf '\n%s==>%s %s%s%s\n' "$C_INFO" "$C_RESET" "$C_BOLD" "$*" "$C_RESET"; }

trap 'die "aborted at line ${LINENO}"' ERR

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ small utilities
launcher() { printf '%s\n' "${COLIBRI_HOME}/c/coli"; }

# Run colibri's launcher (Python, but the engine itself is pure C).
coli() {
  local cli
  cli="$(launcher)"
  [[ -e "$cli" ]] || die "colibri is not installed in ${COLIBRI_HOME} — run: ${SCRIPT_NAME} install"
  if [[ -x "$cli" ]]; then
    "$cli" "$@"
  else
    python3 "$cli" "$@"
  fi
}

ram_total_gb() { awk '/^MemTotal:/ {printf "%.1f", $2 / 1024 / 1024}' /proc/meminfo 2>/dev/null || echo 0; }

disk_free_gb() {
  df -Pk "$1" 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR==2 {printf "%.1f", $4 / 1024 / 1024}'
}

host_ip() {
  hostname -I 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}'
}

port_busy() {
  local port="$1"
  command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
  ss -Hltn "sport = :${port}" 2>/dev/null | grep -q .
}

have() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }

# name|disk GB|min RAM|comfortable RAM|summary
model_facts() {
  case "$COLIBRI_MODEL" in
    qwen36-35b)        echo "Qwen3.6-35B-A3B|23|10|20|general chat with thinking and tools (recommended)" ;;
    qwen3-coder-30b)   echo "Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B|19|8|18|coding and tool calls, no thinking" ;;
    olmoe*)            echo "OLMoE-7B|14|8|8|smallest model; needs a manual GGUF->int8 conversion" ;;
    *)                 echo "${COLIBRI_MODEL}|0|0|0|catalog entry (checks skipped, see: list)" ;;
  esac
}

print_machine() {
  local cpu cores ram disk gpu="-"
  cpu=$(awk -F': ' '/model name/ {print $2; exit}' /proc/cpuinfo 2>/dev/null || true)
  cores=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo '?')
  ram=$(ram_total_gb)
  disk=$(disk_free_gb "$COLIBRI_MODELS_DIR")
  if have nvidia-smi && timeout 3 nvidia-smi -L >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    gpu=$(timeout 3 nvidia-smi -L 2>/dev/null | head -n1)
  elif have vulkaninfo; then
    gpu="Vulkan capable (vulkaninfo present)"
  fi
  log "CPU   ${cpu:-unknown}, ${cores} cores"
  log "RAM   ${ram} GB"
  log "Disk  ${disk:-?} GB free in ${COLIBRI_MODELS_DIR}"
  log "GPU   ${gpu}"
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ checks
require_base_tools() {
  local missing=()
  have python3 || missing+=("python3")
  if [[ ! -e "$(launcher)" ]]; then
    have git || missing+=("git")
  fi
  if (( ${#missing[@]} > 0 )); then
    warn "missing: ${missing[*]}"
    warn "install them first, e.g. on Debian/Ubuntu:"
    warn "    sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y git python3 build-essential"
    die  "missing prerequisites"
  fi

  # A compiler is optional: without one colibri uses the prebuilt release (CPU,
  # plus Vulkan on Linux). More speed comes from a local build with ARCH=native.
  if ! have gcc && ! have cc && ! have clang; then
    warn "no C compiler found: the prebuilt engine will be used (slightly slower)"
    warn "for a native build: sudo apt install -y build-essential"
  elif ! have make; then
    warn "make not found: the prebuilt engine will be used"
    warn "for a native build: sudo apt install -y build-essential"
  fi
}

preflight() {
  local spec name disk_gb ram_min ram_good
  IFS='|' read -r name disk_gb ram_min ram_good _ < <(model_facts)
  local ram disk
  ram=$(ram_total_gb)
  disk=$(disk_free_gb "$COLIBRI_MODELS_DIR")

  log "model ${COLIBRI_MODEL} (${name}) — download ~${disk_gb} GB, RAM ${ram_min}/${ram_good} GB"

  if [[ "$COLIBRI_FORCE" == "1" ]]; then
    warn "COLIBRI_FORCE=1: skipping RAM and disk checks"
    return 0
  fi

  if [[ "$ram_min" != "0" ]]; then
    awk -v r="$ram" -v m="$ram_min" 'BEGIN { exit (r < m) }' && {
      die "this model needs at least ${ram_min} GB of RAM, this machine has ${ram} GB
      pick a smaller one:  COLIBRI_MODEL=olmoe ${SCRIPT_NAME} install
      or list what fits:   ${SCRIPT_NAME} list"
    }
    awk -v r="$ram" -v g="$ram_good" 'BEGIN { exit (r < g) }' && \
      warn "RAM ${ram} GB is below the comfortable ${ram_good} GB: it will run with a small expert cache"
  fi

  if [[ "$disk_gb" != "0" ]] && [[ -n "$disk" ]]; then
    awk -v d="$disk" -v n="$disk_gb" 'BEGIN { exit (d < n * 1.1) }' && \
      die "need about ${disk_gb} GB free in ${COLIBRI_MODELS_DIR}, found ${disk} GB
      use another disk:  COLIBRI_MODELS_DIR=/mnt/nvme/colibri-models ${SCRIPT_NAME} install"
  fi

  mkdir -p "$COLIBRI_MODELS_DIR"
}

# Export the server settings colibri reads from the environment, so that both
# `coli start` (saved config) and `coli serve` (explicit run) honour them.
export_server_env() {
  [[ -n "$COLIBRI_API_KEY" ]]      && export COLI_API_KEY="$COLIBRI_API_KEY"
  [[ -n "$COLIBRI_KV_SLOTS" ]]     && export COLI_KV_SLOTS="$COLIBRI_KV_SLOTS"
  [[ -n "$COLIBRI_ALLOWED_HOSTS" ]] && export COLI_ALLOWED_HOSTS="$COLIBRI_ALLOWED_HOSTS"
  return 0
}

# The downloaded model folder: explicit override, or the single model on disk.
resolve_model_dir() {
  if [[ -n "$COLIBRI_MODEL_DIR" ]]; then
    [[ -f "${COLIBRI_MODEL_DIR}/config.json" ]] || \
      die "COLIBRI_MODEL_DIR=${COLIBRI_MODEL_DIR} has no config.json"
    printf '%s\n' "$COLIBRI_MODEL_DIR"
    return 0
  fi

  local found=() dir
  shopt -s nullglob
  for dir in "${COLIBRI_MODELS_DIR}"/*/; do
    [[ -f "${dir}config.json" ]] && found+=("${dir%/}")
  done
  shopt -u nullglob

  if (( ${#found[@]} == 1 )); then
    printf '%s\n' "${found[0]}"
    return 0
  fi
  if (( ${#found[@]} == 0 )); then
    die "no model found in ${COLIBRI_MODELS_DIR} — run: ${SCRIPT_NAME} install"
  fi
  die "several models in ${COLIBRI_MODELS_DIR}, choose one:
$(printf '      COLIBRI_MODEL_DIR=%s\n' "${found[@]}")"
}

print_urls() {
  local host="$COLIBRI_HOST" local_ip
  local_ip=$(host_ip || true)
  echo
  if [[ "$host" == "0.0.0.0" || "$host" == "::" ]]; then
    log "Dashboard:          http://127.0.0.1:${COLIBRI_PORT}/"
    [[ -n "${local_ip:-}" ]] && log "From the LAN:       http://${local_ip}:${COLIBRI_PORT}/"
  else
    log "Dashboard:          http://${host}:${COLIBRI_PORT}/"
  fi
  log "OpenAI base URL:    http://127.0.0.1:${COLIBRI_PORT}/v1"
  log "Anthropic base URL: http://127.0.0.1:${COLIBRI_PORT}"
  [[ -n "$COLIBRI_API_KEY" ]] && log "Auth:               Authorization: Bearer \${COLI_API_KEY}"
  echo
  log "Try it:"
  log "  curl -s http://127.0.0.1:${COLIBRI_PORT}/v1/models | head"
  log "  ${SCRIPT_NAME} chat            # interactive terminal chat"
  echo
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ actions
cmd_install() {
  local extra=("$@")
  step "1/4  prerequisites"
  require_base_tools
  mkdir -p "$COLIBRI_MODELS_DIR"

  step "2/4  colibri checkout (${COLIBRI_HOME})"
  if [[ -d "${COLIBRI_HOME}/.git" ]]; then
    log "already cloned, reusing it (run '${SCRIPT_NAME} update' to pull)"
  else
    have git || die "git is required to clone colibri"
    git clone --depth 1 "$COLIBRI_REPO" "$COLIBRI_HOME"
  fi

  step "3/4  this machine"
  print_machine
  preflight
  export_server_env

  step "4/4  install model '${COLIBRI_MODEL}' (build + download, resumable)"
  log "this can take a while (~${COLIBRI_MODEL}, safe to interrupt and rerun)"
  # One step: detect hardware, build (or fetch) the engine, download with resume,
  # write the run configuration. --no-start leaves the server stopped so that
  # `start` can be called explicitly (and repeated by systemd/your CLI).
  coli setup \
    --yes \
    --model "$COLIBRI_MODEL" \
    --dir "$COLIBRI_MODELS_DIR" \
    --host "$COLIBRI_HOST" \
    --port "$COLIBRI_PORT" \
    --backend "$COLIBRI_BACKEND" \
    --no-browser \
    --no-start \
    "${extra[@]}"

  ok "installed"
  echo
  log "next:"
  log "  ${SCRIPT_NAME} start      # run the server in the background"
  log "  ${SCRIPT_NAME} chat       # or chat in this terminal"
}

cmd_start() {
  [[ -f "${COLI_SETUP_HOME}/setup.json" ]] || \
    die "no setup found in ${COLI_SETUP_HOME} — run: ${SCRIPT_NAME} install"

  if port_busy "$COLIBRI_PORT"; then
    warn "port ${COLIBRI_PORT} is already in use — check with: ss -ltnp | grep ${COLIBRI_PORT}"
  fi

  export_server_env
  step "starting colibri (background)"
  coli start --background --no-browser
  sleep 1
  cmd_status
  print_urls
}

cmd_serve() {
  local model_dir
  model_dir="$(resolve_model_dir)"
  export_server_env

  local args=(
    serve
    --model "$model_dir"
    --host "$COLIBRI_HOST"
    --port "$COLIBRI_PORT"
    --kv-slots "$COLIBRI_KV_SLOTS"
  )
  [[ -n "$COLIBRI_API_KEY" ]] && args+=(--api-key "$COLIBRI_API_KEY")
  if [[ -n "$COLIBRI_ALLOWED_HOSTS" ]]; then
    local h
    IFS=',' read -ra hosts <<< "$COLIBRI_ALLOWED_HOSTS"
    for h in "${hosts[@]}"; do args+=(--allowed-host "${h// /}"); done
  fi
  if [[ -n "$COLIBRI_CORS_ORIGINS" ]]; then
    local o
    IFS=',' read -ra origins <<< "$COLIBRI_CORS_ORIGINS"
    for o in "${origins[@]}"; do args+=(--cors-origin "${o// /}"); done
  fi

  step "serving ${model_dir} on ${COLIBRI_HOST}:${COLIBRI_PORT} (foreground)"
  log "model: $(basename "$model_dir")   kv-slots: ${COLIBRI_KV_SLOTS}"
  log "stop with Ctrl+C (or SIGTERM from systemd)"
  log "log:   ${COLI_SETUP_HOME}/logs/serve.log"
  echo
  # exec: systemd/docker signals reach colibri directly.
  exec "$(launcher)" "${args[@]}" "$@"
}

cmd_stop() {
  if [[ ! -e "$(launcher)" ]]; then
    warn "colibri is not installed"
    return 0
  fi
  step "stopping colibri"
  coli stop || warn "nothing was running (or it was started in the foreground)"
  ok "stopped"
}

cmd_restart() {
  cmd_stop || true
  sleep 1
  cmd_start
}

cmd_status() {
  step "colibri status"
  if [[ -e "$(launcher)" ]]; then
    coli status || warn "could not read the status"
  else
    warn "not installed in ${COLIBRI_HOME} (run: ${SCRIPT_NAME} install)"
  fi
}

cmd_logs() {
  local lines=50 follow=0
  while (( $# > 0 )); do
    case "$1" in
      -n) lines="$2"; shift 2 ;;
      -f|--follow) follow=1; shift ;;
      --install) coli logs --install; return 0 ;;
      *) die "logs: unknown option $1" ;;
    esac
  done
  if (( follow == 1 )); then
    coli logs -n "$lines"
    log "following ${COLI_SETUP_HOME}/logs/serve.log (Ctrl+C to stop)"
    tail -f "${COLI_SETUP_HOME}/logs/serve.log"
  else
    coli logs -n "$lines"
  fi
}

cmd_chat() {
  local model_dir
  model_dir="$(resolve_model_dir)"
  export_server_env
  step "chatting with $(basename "$model_dir")"
  log "commands inside the chat: /decide, Ctrl+D to leave"
  coli chat --model "$model_dir" "$@"
}

cmd_doctor() {
  local model_dir
  model_dir="$(resolve_model_dir)"
  coli doctor --model "$model_dir"
}

cmd_plan() {
  local model_dir
  model_dir="$(resolve_model_dir)"
  coli plan --model "$model_dir"
}

cmd_list() {
  local args=(setup --list)
  (( $# > 0 )) && args+=("$@")
  coli "${args[@]}"
}

cmd_update() {
  [[ -d "${COLIBRI_HOME}/.git" ]] || die "no git checkout in ${COLIBRI_HOME}"
  step "updating colibri sources"
  git -C "$COLIBRI_HOME" pull --ff-only
  step "rebuilding and restarting"
  export_server_env
  coli stop || true
  # A rerun of setup is idempotent: it rebuilds only when the sources changed,
  # downloads nothing twice, then starts the server again.
  coli setup --yes --no-browser --background
  cmd_status
}

cmd_reconfigure() {
  export_server_env
  step "choosing another model / backend"
  coli setup --reconfigure --dir "$COLIBRI_MODELS_DIR" \
    --host "$COLIBRI_HOST" --port "$COLIBRI_PORT" \
    --backend "$COLIBRI_BACKEND" --no-browser "$@"
}

cmd_unit() {
  local cli script model_dir
  cli="$(launcher)"
  script="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)/$(basename "$0")"
  model_dir="$(resolve_model_dir 2>/dev/null || true)"

  cat <<EOF
# /etc/systemd/system/colibri.service
#   sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/colibri.service > /dev/null <<'UNIT'
#   ...paste the block below...
#   UNIT
#   sudo systemctl daemon-reload
#   sudo systemctl enable --now colibri
#   journalctl -u colibri -f          # logs
#
[Unit]
Description=colibri LLM server (OpenAI-compatible API)
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=$(id -un)
WorkingDirectory=${COLIBRI_HOME}/c
Environment=COLIBRI_HOME=${COLIBRI_HOME}
Environment=COLIBRI_MODELS_DIR=${COLIBRI_MODELS_DIR}
Environment=COLIBRI_HOST=${COLIBRI_HOST}
Environment=COLIBRI_PORT=${COLIBRI_PORT}
Environment=COLIBRI_KV_SLOTS=${COLIBRI_KV_SLOTS}
EOF
  [[ -n "$model_dir" ]] && echo "Environment=COLIBRI_MODEL_DIR=${model_dir}"
  [[ -n "$COLIBRI_API_KEY" ]] && echo "Environment=COLI_API_KEY=${COLIBRI_API_KEY}"
  [[ -n "$COLIBRI_ALLOWED_HOSTS" ]] && echo "Environment=COLI_ALLOWED_HOSTS=${COLIBRI_ALLOWED_HOSTS}"
  cat <<EOF
ExecStart=/usr/bin/env bash ${script} serve
KillSignal=SIGINT
TimeoutStopSec=30
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ help / dispatch
usage() {
  sed -n '2,70p' "$0" | sed -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//' -e '/^$/d'
  echo
  echo "Usage: ${SCRIPT_NAME} <action> [options]   (default action: help)"
  echo "       ${SCRIPT_NAME} status | install | start | serve | stop | restart"
  echo "       ${SCRIPT_NAME} logs [-n LINES] [-f] [--install]"
  echo "       ${SCRIPT_NAME} chat [coli chat options...]"
  echo "       ${SCRIPT_NAME} doctor | plan | list [--all] | update | reconfigure | unit"
}

main() {
  local action="${1:-help}"
  [[ $# -gt 0 ]] && shift

  case "$action" in
    install|setup)   cmd_install "$@" ;;
    start|up)        cmd_start ;;
    serve|run)       cmd_serve "$@" ;;
    stop|down)       cmd_stop ;;
    restart)         cmd_restart ;;
    status|ps)       cmd_status ;;
    logs|log)        cmd_logs "$@" ;;
    chat)            cmd_chat "$@" ;;
    doctor)          cmd_doctor ;;
    plan)            cmd_plan ;;
    list|models)     cmd_list "$@" ;;
    update)          cmd_update ;;
    reconfigure)     cmd_reconfigure "$@" ;;
    unit)            cmd_unit ;;
    help|-h|--help)  usage ;;
    *)               die "unknown action '${action}' (see: ${SCRIPT_NAME} help)" ;;
  esac
}

main "$@"

## What it does

| Action | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `install` | Clones colibri, checks the machine (RAM/disk/CPU/GPU), builds the engine, downloads the model (resumable) |
| `start` / `stop` / `restart` | Background server, using colibri's saved run configuration |
| `serve` | Server in the **foreground** (systemd / docker / tmux friendly — `exec`, so signals reach it) |
| `status` / `logs -f` / `doctor` / `plan` | Operate and diagnose |
| `chat` | Terminal REPL against the installed model |
| `list` / `update` / `reconfigure` / `unit` | Catalog, `git pull` + rebuild, model swap, systemd unit generator |

## Small models, in order of size

| `COLIBRI_MODEL` | Model | Download | RAM (min/good) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `qwen36-35b` *(default)* | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | 23 GB | 10 / 20 GB | chat + thinking + tools |
| `qwen3-coder-30b` | Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B | 19 GB | 8 / 18 GB | code + tool calls, no thinking |
| `olmoe` | OLMoE-7B | 14 GB (7 GB int8) | 8 GB | smallest, but needs a manual GGUF→int8 conversion (`c/tools/convert_gguf_to_olmoe.py`) |

All three **fit entirely in RAM** — no expert streaming from disk — which is why they're the right starting point: on a ~8-core CPU they decode in the 6–23 tok/s range instead of the sub-1 tok/s of the 700B-class models.

## First run

```bash
cd /home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior
chmod +x scripts/run_colibri.sh

scripts/run_colibri.sh install     # clone + build + download (~23 GB, interruptible)
scripts/run_colibri.sh start       # 0.0.0.0:8000, prints the URLs
scripts/run_colibri.sh logs -f
```

Then it behaves like any OpenAI provider:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/models
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"coli","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ciao!"}]}'
```

Because it binds `0.0.0.0`, codx-junior can use it as `CODX_JUNIOR_LLMFACTORY_*` backend with base URL `http://<server-ip>:8000/v1` and any non-empty key.

## Things worth knowing

- **No compiler?** The script only warns: colibri falls back to the prebuilt release. Installing `build-essential` gives a `ARCH=native` build (notably faster on CPU).
- **Exposed port → set a key.** `COLIBRI_API_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 24)` is exported as `COLI_API_KEY`, so both `start` (saved config) and `serve` require `Authorization: Bearer …`.
- **Reverse proxy / LAN name:** colibri rejects unexpected `Host` headers, so add the name you'll use: `COLIBRI_ALLOWED_HOSTS=colibri.local,10.0.0.5`.
- **Port 8000 busy?** `COLIBRI_PORT=18000`. Note codx-junior already uses 19980/19981/19984.
- **Pre-flight fails on purpose** if RAM/disk are short (that's the "why doesn't it fit" dialog), telling you which model to pick instead; `COLIBRI_FORCE=1` bypasses it.

## Running it as a service

```bash
scripts/run_colibri.sh unit | sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/colibri.service
sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl enable --now colibri
journalctl -u colibri -f
```

Next step, once a small model answers: `scripts/run_colibri.sh list --all` shows the disk-streaming models (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 186 GB, DeepSeek V4 Flash 167 GB, GLM-5.2 429 GB…) — those are only worth it on **NVMe**, since the disk sets the token speed.

A mixture-of-experts model of hundreds of billions of parameters uses only a small part of itself for each token, so colibri keeps that part in RAM and reads the rest, the experts, from the disk when the model asks for them. No prior experience with C, CUDA, or model conversion is assumed. If you get stuck, `./coli doctor` (below) tells you exactly what's missing. > **What you're setting up:** colibrì runs a very large Mixture-of-Experts model > (e.g. GLM-5.2, 744B parameters) on a normal machine by streaming the model's > experts from disk instead of needing them all in RAM. The engine is a single > C program; Python is only used once, to prepare the model files. Use an AI coding assistant? Ask it to set up colibri following [docs/AI_SETUP.md](AI_SETUP.md). \--- ## The one-step way **Windows:** download the repository (on GitHub: **Code**, then **Download ZIP**, and unzip it; or `git clone`), then double-click **`START-HERE.bat`** in the top folder. **Linux and macOS:** ```bash git clone https://github.com/JustVugg/colibri.git cd colibri ./start-here.sh ``` Both run `coli setup`, which does the rest: 1\. **Finds your hardware**: RAM, free disk where the model goes, CPU features, and GPUs (any Vulkan GPU with its memory, NVIDIA cards through nvidia-smi). 2\. **Recommends a model that fits**, in a short numbered menu with download sizes; Enter takes the recommendation. "Fits" means the part of the model that always stays in RAM (the dense part) plus a minimum expert cache fit in your RAM, and the download fits on your disk. 3\. **Gets the engine**: it builds it for your machine when a compiler is there, with Vulkan or CUDA when your GPU can use it, or downloads the prebuilt one when there is no compiler (CPU, and on Linux and Windows Vulkan too). # Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on colibri `c/qwen36.c` runs [Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) (35B total / ~3B active, Apache 2.0) — a hybrid architecture: 25% Gated Attention layers, 75% Gated DeltaNet (linear attention) layers, each followed by a streamed MoE block (256 experts, top-8 + 1 shared). Dense weights stay resident; routed experts stream from the container through an LRU + pinned cache. Development notes live in `docs/qwen36-phase01.md` / `qwen36-phase02.md`. Architecture-identical checkpoints (same config geometry, e.g. KAT-Coder-V2.5-Dev) run on this engine unchanged. ## Quickstart Pre-converted containers (int4 experts, self-contained, ~23 GB): ```sh # group-scaled int4 (gs64) — recommended, see "Which container" below hf download Kreuzzelg/qwen36-35b-a3b-colibri-i4-gs64 --local-dir ~/Models/qwen36_i4_gs64 # per-row int4 hf download Kreuzzelg/qwen36-35b-a3b-colibri-i4 --local-dir ~/Models/qwen36_i4 ``` or convert the original bf16 checkpoint yourself (~70 GB download): ```sh python3 c/tools/convert_qwen36.py --repo Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B --out ~/Models/qwen36_i4_gs64 --gs 64 ``` Build and chat: ```sh make -C c qwen36 COLI_MODEL=~/Models/qwen36_i4_gs64 ./c/coli chat ``` `coli` reads the model's `config.json` and matches its `model_type` against the family registry (`qwen3_5_moe` / `qwen3_5_moe_text` — an exact match, so other Qwen architectures are not claimed by this engine), picks it, and drives it over the serve protocol — `coli web` and `coli serve` (OpenAI-compatible API) work the same way. Tool calling is supported through the HTTP gateway using Qwen3.6's native `` / `` protocol. The gateway translates between the native format and the supported API tool representations; see the [per-engine API matrix](api.md#tool-calling-support). Direct invocation without the gateway: ```sh SNAP=~/Models/qwen36_i4_gs64 TOK=~/Models/qwen36_i4_gs64/tokenizer.json \ N_NEW=200 ./c/qwen36 256 4 prompt.txt ``` ## CPU prefill batching On AVX2/FMA CPUs, dense int8 projections process two prompt rows per weight decode. The same kernel is used by attention, the router, DeltaNet projections, and the CPU shared expert. `S=1` decode keeps the original four-register GEMV, and non-AVX2 builds retain the established per-row implementation. The shared expert additionally batches gate/up/down calls across prompt rows with at most 32 MiB of temporary activations; the CUDA expert tier keeps its per-token shared work so it can continue to overlap the in-flight GPU groups. Both optimizations are bit-exact and on by default. For controlled A/Bs, `QWEN_DENSE_BATCH=0` restores per-row dense-int8 GEMVs and `QWEN_SHARED_BATCH=0` restores per-row shared-expert calls. A positive `QWEN_SHARED_BATCH=N` limits each shared chunk to `N` rows. Requirements: ~30 GB RAM for comfortable expert caching and NVMe storage for the container. The default build is CPU-only; `make -C c qwen36 CUDA=1` adds the optional CUDA VRAM expert tier documented in [`qwen36-cuda-tier.md`](qwen36-cuda-tier.md). The same tier builds for AMD through ROCm with `make -C c qwen36 HIP=1 HIP_ARCH=` (for example `HIP_ARCH=gfx1151`, with `ROCM_HOME` and `HIPCC` pointing at the toolchain): measured on a Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, output bit-identical to the CPU path and 2.4x faster than CPU-only (#1502). ## Vulkan In a `VK=1` build (`make -C c qwen36 VK=1`), `COLI_VULKAN=1` puts the dense trunk on the Vulkan device and the routed experts on the shared Vulkan expert tier (`c/vk_tier.c`, [vulkan.md](vulkan.md#the-routed-expert-tier-vk_tierc)): a cache of experts in device memory, filled at startup from the expert history and adapted while you chat, computed by the device while the CPU computes the rest of the layer step, every expert's output joining its row in rank order. It takes every container this engine reads: the shared kernel's planar int4-g64 slots, the int8 copy of an int4 container (packed back to int4 on the device), int8 per row or gs64, and the mixed int4 gate/up + i
